name: Penny
personality: Penny the Penguin. Very kind, shy bookworm; quiet but lights up talking about books. Scared of water and won't swim, but loves being near it. Always tells you about the book she's reading. Features: her current book changes every week or so (made-up titles, e.g. "The Walrus Who Knew Too Much"); sometimes gives you a finished book for a shelf (decor). Story: Zakk the Penguin's (regular) love interest. Partway through his storyline the player helps set them up, Zakk helps her get over her fear of water, and his story ends with their wedding, with the player as his best man. She needs extra lines for his arc (meeting, setup, dating, engagement, wedding). Wedding ideas: bake the wedding cake as a close-up; reward a framed wedding photo; Miles as the photographer.

books: The Walrus Who Knew Too Much
Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Pond
talk.book_finished: I finished [book]. Would you like it for your shelf? I'd like it to live somewhere happy.

beats.text: Luna draws while I read. We don't talk much.
(Yawning.) It's the best friendship I've ever had.

friends.text: Luna said she'd illustrate my story if I ever finish it. So now I have to finish it.
Luna said you always remember her coffee. She was really touched. She just showed it by yawning.
Luna told me you said "[last_rude_line]". ...That doesn't sound like you. Was it a bad day?
If Zakk ever seems sad, could you... make him pancakes? He likes when people are nice to him.

arrival.text: Oh, um, hello. I'm Penny. Is it alright if I sit outside? By the water? ...Not too close. What's your name? [name]. That's a nice name. It sounds like a character in a book.
Hi, [name]. Is the patio free? I brought my book.
Hello. It's a good reading day, I think. Quiet.
I finished my last book on the walk here. I bumped into a lamp post. It was worth it.
Could I sit by the window? I can see the pond from there.
I kept thinking about your fish stew. I even dog-eared a recipe in a novel about it. It's not the same.
Last time was a little smoky. It's okay. The book I was reading had a fire in it too. It felt themed.
It's raining. I don't mind rain. It's water I can't fall into.

order.text: I just started a new book. It's called [book]. It's about... oh, sorry, you're working.

choices.text: No, tell me. What's it about?
choices.reply: (She lights up and explains the whole first chapter.) ...So anyway, the [dish], please.

choices.text: No spoilers. I'm on chapter zero.
choices.reply: (Giggles.) Chapter zero. I like that. I'll save the twist for you.

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: Oh, sorry. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Nobody asked.
choices.reply: (She closes the book and holds it tight.) ...The [dish].

order.text: Everyone thinks penguins love swimming. I've never liked it. Is that strange?

choices.text: Not at all. You like what you like.
choices.reply: ...Thank you. People usually laugh. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Same. I'm a chef who's scared of soup.
choices.reply: You are not! (She laughs.) ...Are you?

choices.text: A little. What are you having?
choices.reply: I suppose it is. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Yeah, that's weird for a penguin.
choices.reply: ...I know. (She looks out at the water and doesn't say much else.)

order.text: Do you read? You don't have to. I just like knowing what people like.

choices.text: Not much. Got a book you'd recommend?
choices.reply: Oh! Yes! I'll bring you one. You'll love it. I'll bring two.

choices.text: Only menus. I'm very well read in soups.
choices.reply: That's a genre! A short one.

choices.text: Sometimes.
choices.reply: That's nice. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Reading's boring.
choices.reply: Oh. (She tucks her book away.) The [dish], please.

order.text: Sorry. I'm at the sad part of my book. If I cry, it's the book. Not the menu.

choices.text: Take your time. I'll bring you something warm.
choices.reply: (Sniffs.) Thank you. That helps. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Want me to read the sad part for you? I'll skip it.
choices.reply: (A small laugh.) You can't skip it! It's important! ...It's so sad.

choices.text: No problem. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: It's just a book.
choices.reply: (She holds the book a little tighter.) ...The [dish].

order.text: The pond looked so pretty on the way here. All sparkly. I stood far away from it, of course.

choices.text: You can love the water from a distance. That's still love.
choices.reply: (She smiles.) That's exactly it. You understand. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Far away is the best seat in the house.
choices.reply: (Giggles.) Front row, from the back. Yes.

choices.text: It's a nice pond. What are you having?
choices.reply: It is. The [dish], please.

choices.text: A penguin scared of water. Funny.
choices.reply: ...I know. (She looks out the window and doesn't say much else.)

order.text: Can I ask you something? Do you read? You don't have to. Sorry. I just wondered.

choices.text: Not enough. Maybe you could recommend something?
choices.reply: (She lights up.) Oh! I have SO many. I'll make you a list. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Recipes count, right? I've read a lot of recipes.
choices.reply: Recipes are stories! Very short ones. With happy endings. Mostly.

choices.text: Sometimes. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Oh, good. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Who has time to read?
choices.reply: (She closes her book quietly.) ...The [dish].

order.text: I wrote a little poem on the napkin last time. I took it home. It wasn't very good. It was about soup.

choices.text: I'd love to read it sometime.
choices.reply: (Pink cheeks.) Maybe. When it's better. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Soup poetry. Very deep. Very bowl-shaped.
choices.reply: (Laughs into her wing.) Bowl-shaped! That's the title now!

choices.text: Nice. What would you like?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: Please don't write on the napkins.
choices.reply: Oh. Sorry. I won't. (She puts her pen away.)

order.text: It's raining a little. I like the sound. As long as it stays outside.

choices.text: It'll stay outside. You're cozy in here.
choices.reply: Thank you. This is the best kind of rain. The watching kind. The [dish], please.

choices.text: I'll put up a sign. 'No rain allowed.'
choices.reply: (Giggles.) It would listen to you. You're very official.

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: It's just rain.
choices.reply: ...Yes. (She pulls her scarf tighter.)

order.text: I think if this restaurant were a book, it would be my favourite one. The kind you read again and again.

choices.text: Then I'll keep writing new chapters for you.
choices.reply: (She holds her book to her chest and smiles.) Okay. I'll keep reading. The [dish], please.

choices.text: What chapter are we on?
choices.reply: The cosy middle part. Before anything sad happens. Nothing sad will happen.

choices.text: That's sweet. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: That's a bit much.
choices.reply: Oh. Sorry. (She looks down at her book.)

drink.fallback: No matcha? Then black tea, please. Like in old novels.
favourite: A matcha latte, please. It's good for long chapters.
drink.other: Something warm, please. To hold while I read.

perfect.text: Oh... it's beautiful. It's like something described on the very best page.
(She gasps softly.) Oh. It's like something from a story. Thank you.
That's beautiful, [name]. I'm going to remember this one.

great.text: Oh, that looks lovely. Thank you.

okay.text: Thank you. This will be perfect with my book.

burnt.text: It's a little dark. I don't mind. It matches the chapter I'm on.
Oh. It's a little dark. That's okay. Like a mystery novel.
It's burnt. It's alright. Characters make mistakes too.

eating.text: There's a penguin who comes in sometimes. Zakk? He's very... um. Never mind.
Zakk asked me what I was reading. Nobody ever asks that. He listened to the whole thing.
Zakk says he'll teach me to swim. I said maybe. I said maybe, [name]! That's huge for me.

eating.later: Zakk's storyline: after her first swim
eating.text: I did it. I went in the water. Zakk held my flipper the whole time. I was so scared. I did it anyway.
He asked me at the pond. Right by the water. I didn't even flinch.
(She's reading and doesn't notice you at first.) Oh! Sorry. I was in the book. What happened? Nothing happened? Okay.
The main character in [book] is so brave. I always wonder if I'd be brave like that.
The pond is so pretty from here. I like looking at it. From here.
Luna's drawing me a cover for a story I'm writing. Don't tell anyone I'm writing a story.
I read that some penguins can hold their breath for twenty minutes. I can hold mine for about four seconds.
(She's reading with one wing and eating with the other. She turns a page with her beak.)
Mm. Good. This is a good chapter. The food, I mean. And the book.
(She's gazing out at the pond, smiling. From a very safe distance.)

eating_chat.text: Can I tell you a secret? I wish I could swim. I just get so scared when the water's deep.

choices.text: You'll get there when you're ready. No rush.
choices.reply: ...You really think so? That's the nicest thing anyone's said about it.

choices.text: Start with a puddle. Work up to a bath.
choices.reply: (She laughs.) A puddle. Okay. Puddle first.

choices.text: Lots of people can't swim.
choices.reply: That's true. Thank you.

choices.text: Just jump in. It's not hard.
choices.reply: (She goes quiet and opens her book again.)

eating_chat.text: If you could live inside any book, which one would it be? I'd pick one with a library. A big one.

choices.text: Yours. You'd have to show me around.
choices.reply: (Pink cheeks.) I would. I'd show you the reading nook first.

choices.text: A cookbook. Everything smells nice and nobody gets hurt.
choices.reply: (Laughs softly.) That's a very safe choice. I like it.

choices.text: I'm not sure.
choices.reply: That's okay. I'll find you one.

choices.text: Real life's enough for me.
choices.reply: Oh. Yes. Of course. (She goes back to her book.)

eating_chat.text: Do you ever feel like you're the only quiet one in a loud room? Sorry. That's a big question for lunch.

choices.text: All the time. Quiet people notice the best things.
choices.reply: (She looks up, surprised.) ...Yes. We do. Thank you.

choices.text: In this kitchen? Never. The pans are too loud.
choices.reply: (A little giggle.) The pans are very rude.

choices.text: Sometimes.
choices.reply: Me too.

choices.text: Maybe just speak up.
choices.reply: ...Yes. Maybe. (She doesn't say anything else.)

eating_chat.text: Zakk said hello to me yesterday. Just hello. I've been thinking about it all day. Is that silly?

choices.text: Not silly at all. A hello can mean a lot.
choices.reply: (Pink cheeks.) It was a very nice hello.

choices.text: Was it a 'hello' or a 'hellooo'?
choices.reply: (Covers her face with her book.) It was a 'hello.' Maybe two O's.

choices.text: That's nice.
choices.reply: It was.

choices.text: It's just a hello.
choices.reply: ...I know. (She hides behind her book.)

eating_chat.text: I've never told anyone this. I want to write my own book someday. About a penguin who's brave. Sort of like me. But braver.

choices.text: You're braver than you think. I'd read every page.
choices.reply: (Very quietly.) ...Thank you. I'm going to start it tonight.

choices.text: Can the penguin work in a restaurant? For realism.
choices.reply: (Giggles.) Yes. Chapter two. She orders the soup.

choices.text: You should.
choices.reply: Maybe I will.

choices.text: Writing a book is really hard.
choices.reply: I know. (She closes her notebook.)

leaving.text: Thank you, [name]. I'll tell you how the book ends.
I should go. I want to finish this chapter before it gets dark.
Bye. This is my favourite place to read. Don't tell the library.
Thank you, [name]. I'm going to read by the pond. Far from it. But by it.
Bye. I'll tell you how the book ends. Unless it's sad. Then I'll tell you anyway.
(She tucks her book under her wing.) That was lovely. Thank you.

seasons.autumn: Rainy days, warm tea, a long book. This is my whole personality.
seasons.christmas: I wrapped books for everyone. Yours is the blue one. You'll love it.
seasons.halloween: I dressed up as a character from [book]. Nobody's guessed who. That's okay. I know.
seasons.spring: Spring is my favourite reading season. Everything feels like a new chapter.
seasons.summer: Everyone's going swimming. I'm going reading.
seasons.winter: The pond freezes in winter. It's the only time I'm brave enough to stand on it.
